words.definition: to become less strong or less severe; to ease off gradually.
words.exampleSentence: By morning the storm had abated, and the crews went back out on the water.

words.definition: bubbling over with cheerful energy; loudly and visibly enthusiastic.
words.exampleSentence: The ebullient crowd cheered every runner who crossed the finish line, first or last.

words.definition: saying a great deal in very few words; clipped and brief in speech.
words.exampleSentence: Her laconic reply — just the word 'noted' — ended the meeting on the spot.

words.definition: to cloud or muddle something so it is harder to understand, usually on purpose.
words.exampleSentence: The report seemed designed to obfuscate the numbers rather than explain them.
